description: Publishes a spec on Spekkr under the signed-in person's username, as username/name, or publishes a new version of one of theirs. Send the text of spekkr.json and every file it lists. A small text file goes in files with its content. Any other file (an image, a PDF, a video, a long document) goes in files with its size in bytes and no content: the answer then gives an address to upload those files to with HTTP PUT, and once they are uploaded you call publish_spec again with the same arguments. Nothing is listed until a call answers with published. A listed spec names the member who published it. A published version never changes: to update a spec, raise the version, add a changelog entry and list every file again. A file that has not changed goes in files with keep set to true and nothing else, and Spekkr takes it from the version listed now, so a screenshot need not be uploaded again. Earlier versions stay on Spekkr and can still be pulled. For a fork that fork_spec started, pass its keepFrom as well: kept files then come from the spec it was forked from. In this version a published spec is free. If anything has to change first, the answer names every problem. The answer may carry advice on the text, as check_spec gives it; advice does not stop the publish. This tool needs sign-in. Ask the person before you call it: publishing makes the files public.

files.description: Every file the manifest lists, every file inside a folder it lists, and every screenshot under demo.screenshots. Leave out spekkr.json, BUILD.md and spekkr.inputs.json. Each file has a path and one of content, bytes or keep.

bytes.description: The file's exact size in bytes, for a file that will be uploaded: one that is not text, or is too long to send as content. Up to 25,000,000.

content.description: The file's whole text. For text files of up to 200,000 bytes.

keep.description: True for a file that is the same as in the version listed now, or, with keepFrom, as in that spec. Give no content or bytes with it.

path.description: The file's path inside the spec's folder, like spec.md or shots/home.png.

keepFrom.description: The id of the spec that kept files are taken from, when it is not this spec: the one the manifest names under lineage.forkedFrom. fork_spec gives it. Leave it out for a new version of one of the person's own specs.

manifest.description: The whole text of the spec's spekkr.json. Its id is username/name, with the signed-in person's username, and its author.id is that username.

name: publish_spec
title: Publish a spec
